uncited: Basic Primitive Definitions provide the foundational analytical Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) for simple geometric shapes, serving as the atomic building blocks for distance-field ray marching.
They compute the exact Euclidean distance from a query point to the surface of a shape, guaranteeing no underestimation to prevent ray overshooting.

Unlike [SDF Domain Manipulation Operators](1730-sdf-domain-manipulation-operators.md) which transform space or [SDF Rounding](1829-sdf-rounding.md) which modifies surfaces, primitives define the base geometry itself [S7, unofficial].
**Canonical Definition**: Primitives are defined centered at the origin with specific orientations (e.g., sphere at $(0,0,0)$, cylinder along Y-axis) [S7, unofficial].
**Output**: A scalar signed distance $d \in \mathbb{R}$, where $d < 0$ indicates inside and $d > 0$ indicates outside [S7, unofficial].

The concept of using analytical distance functions for rendering was popularized by Inigo Quilez in his online tutorials, providing efficient, branch-free distance estimators for ray marching [S1, S3, S5, S6, S7, unofficial].
These primitives form the core of modern SDF-based rendering, enabling complex scene construction through boolean operations and domain manipulation.
